newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa shifts hospital ahead of heart test.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa shifts hospital ahead of heart test.

text.p: Mother Teresa, in intensive care with recurrent chest pain, was moved to an Indian heart clinic on Tuesday after she agreed to undergo a special X-ray test to see if surgery is necessary, her doctor said.

Dr S.K. Sen of the Woodlands Nursing Home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta said the 86-year-old nun had been moved to the nearby clinic for an angiography, an X-ray of blood vessels to see if she has a blocked artery.

A hushed crowd of about 200 people, including nuns from her Missionaries of Charity religious order, watched Mother Teresa, eyes shut and arms folded over her chest, as she was carried from the hospital on a stretcher.
A doctor, a nurse and four nuns escorted her in the ambulance on the short drive to B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre.
"Generally she is alright," said A.K. Chatterjee, the heart clinic administrator. "She has been placed in the critical care unit where all heart support arrangements are available."
Chatterjee said a team of doctors would fix the date of the angiography, which he said would likely take place on Wednesday.
"A team of doctors is investigating and they will decide when Mother Teresa will undergo angiography," he said.
Mother Teresa, fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, has twice undergone coronary angiography -- once in 1991 in the United States and a second time in 1993 at the Birla clinic.
In both cases she subsequently underwent angioplasty, in which surgeons inserted a balloon into her artery to unblock it.
Woodlands Nursing Home said in a medical bulletin that the results of the angiography would show if she needed angioplasty.
Sen told reporters Mother Teresa had another bout of chest pain on Tuesday afternoon, which briefly delayed her transfer to the clinic.

"Mother had another round of chest pain this afternoon," Sen said. "All arrangements had been made for her transfer. Even the doctors, nurses and ambulance had come. But we had to wait for the fresh bout of chest pain to subside."
Dr Patricia Aubanel, who treated her in the United States, had arrived in Calcutta to supervise the procedure, he added.
Known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the world's downtrodden, the 86-year-old nun was admitted to hospital with an irregular heart-beat early on Friday.

Mother Teresa, who has ischaemia, or hardening of the arteries, has suffered heart failure three times since last Thursday. But on Monday she had shown some reluctance to undergo any special tests or surgery.

Sen said angiography was a very safe procedure involving the injection of dye through a catheter. The dye shows up on the X-ray, revealing any blockage. The patient will be put under general anaesthesia, Sen said.
Earlier on Tuesday, Mother Teresa's cardiologist said her persistent irregular heart beat was worrying, but that she was reluctant to undergo surgery.
"When she agreed, we decided to do it quickly unless she might change her decision," Sen said.
The two doctors who performed angioplasty on Mother Teresa at the Birla centre in 1993, Dr Deepak Shetty and Dr Tarun Praharaj, will conduct the angiography, Sen said.
